name: Orís (Spain)
description: Red field charged at the centre with one of the white scallop shells of the arms, within a bordure of 36 square pieces alternately yellow and black.
history: The flag is drawn from the arms (approved 24 May 1984, DOGC no. 451 of 11 July 1984), which show the castle of the village on a hill and two scallops from the arms of the Orís family, lords of the castle. The council approved the flag on 9 December 2003 and it was published in the DOGC on 29 January 2004: an oblong flag of 2:3, red, with one of the white scallops of the arms 3/5 of the height at the centre and a bordure of 36 square pieces alternately yellow and black.
